prompt.context: Your client is HealthCo, a software company that has developed an innovative software solution for hospitals. The software is used for tracking patient outcomes and utilizes an extensive database and proprietary analytics to recommend procedures based on patient comorbidities. HealthCo is preparing to go to market and is seeking our advice on how to maximize revenue.
prompt.question: How should HealthCo price its software to maximize revenue?

clarifying_info.a: Software is provided to hospitals for a fixed annual fee, independent of the number of patients served or doctors using it.
The software is patented and there are currently no competitors in the market.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's primary objective?
clarifying_info.a: The client is focused on maximizing revenue.

clarifying_info.q: How many patients does each hospital serve annually?
clarifying_info.a: Small hospitals: 5,000 patients; Medium hospitals: 10,000 patients; Large hospitals: 15,000 patients.

clarifying_info.q: What is the value of the software per patient by hospital size?
clarifying_info.a: Small: $50 per patient; Medium: $30 per patient; Large: $10 per patient.

exhibits.title: Hospital distribution by size
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage distribution of 5,400 total hospitals across three size categories: Small, Medium, and Large.

framework: Recognize this is a Market Entry / Pricing case
Identify that pricing should be based on value the software brings to each hospital
Segment hospitals by size and calculate maximum willingness to pay per segment
Determine the number of hospitals in each segment using the exhibit
Calculate total revenue at each possible price point (set at each segment's willingness to pay)
Select the price that maximizes total revenue
Address network effects, risks, next steps, and recommendation

questions.prompt: Calculate the number of hospitals in each size segment.
questions.guidance: Use total hospitals (5,400) and the percentage distribution from Exhibit 1: Small = 55.6%, Medium = 33.3%, Large = 11.1%.

questions.prompt: Calculate the maximum willingness to pay for each hospital size segment.
questions.guidance: Multiply annual patients per hospital by value per patient for each segment. A strong candidate notes that large hospitals see more patients and can generate their own sample-size-based recommendations, so the incremental value of the software is lower for them.

math.setup: Willingness to pay = patients per hospital * value per patient

questions.prompt: Calculate total revenue at each of the three candidate price points ($150k, $250k, $300k) and identify the revenue-maximizing price.
questions.guidance: At each price point, only hospitals whose willingness to pay is at or above that price will purchase. Candidate must correctly identify which segments buy at each price and multiply by number of hospitals.

math.setup: Hospitals buy only if price <= their maximum willingness to pay. Segment WTP: Large=$150k, Small=$250k, Medium=$300k.
steps: Price $150k: All three segments buy. Revenue = $150k * (3,000+1,800+600) = $150k * 5,400 = $810M
Price $250k: Small and Medium buy (Large will not, as $250k > $150k WTP). Revenue = $250k * (3,000+1,800) = $250k * 4,800 = $1,200M

brainstorming.prompt: What additional considerations or risks should HealthCo keep in mind as it goes to market?

categories.name: Network Effects
ideas: Software value is significantly based on total number of users across hospitals
A larger aggregate dataset improves analytics and recommendations
Pricing may be increased after a large installed base is established

categories.name: Adoption Risks
ideas: Hospitals may be slow to adopt new technology
Insufficient adoption could prevent hospitals from achieving maximum value
Training and change management costs for hospital staff

categories.name: Growth Opportunities
ideas: Develop software for other patient service institutions such as physical therapy, primary care physicians, etc.
Add modules or features to upsell existing customers

categories.name: Competitive Risks
ideas: Patent protection is finite; competitors may enter after expiry
Large hospitals with internal analytics capabilities may build competing solutions

recommendation: Price the software at $250k per hospital per year to achieve maximum annual revenue of $1.2B
This price captures all Small and Medium hospitals while excluding Large hospitals whose willingness to pay is only $150k
risks: Insufficient adoption — hospitals may not achieve the maximum value the pricing assumes
Large hospitals excluded at this price point may develop or adopt competing solutions once the patent expires
next_steps: Hire and train a dedicated hospital sales team
Develop a marketing pitch that demonstrates quantified value for hospitals by size
Explore expanding the software to other patient-service institutions such as physical therapy clinics and primary care physicians
Monitor adoption rates and consider a tiered or network-effect-based pricing increase once a large installed base is established
